BiblicalUsage: maltâʻâh is a grinder, a back tooth, and it occurs once, in the psalmist's prayer in Psalms 58:6. There he asks God to break the teeth of the wicked in their mouth and to break out the great teeth of the young lions. The word is the tooth that crushes, and the prayer asks God to take its power away.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe maltâʻâh reminds me that God can break the strength of those who tear others apart, and that prayer is the right place to ask Him to do it.
